nodes.summary: The average linkage between two clusters: the mean of `d x y` over `x ∈ C`, `y ∈ D`.
nodes.title: Average linkage between clusters

nodes.summary: Bootstrap support is a frequency: it lies in `[0, 1]`.
nodes.title: Bootstrap support lies in the unit interval

nodes.summary: Bootstrap support (Felsenstein 1985) of the split with side `A` away from `a`, for a tree estimator `est` and an alignment `M` of `m` sites: the fraction of the `m ^ m` site resamplings with replacement `w : Fin m → Fin m` (uniform draws, whose site counts are multinomial) for which the tree estimated from the resampled alignment `M ∘ w` has the cluster `A`. This is the exact bootstrap proportion; Felsenstein's…
nodes.title: Bootstrap support

nodes.summary: Correctness of BUILD (Aho, Sagiv, Szymanski & Ullman 1981; Semple & Steel 2003, Section 6.4): a set `R` of triplets on a nonempty `S`, none of the degenerate form `xx|x` (which no tree displays and no cut detects), is displayed by a rooted binary phylogenetic tree on `S` iff for every subset `S'` of at least two taxa the Aho graph of `R` on `S'` is disconnected. BUILD splits along the components and recurses; the…
nodes.title: Correctness of BUILD

nodes.summary: A binary hierarchy on `S` has `2 |S| - 1` members: the `|S|` singletons and `|S| - 1` internal clusters (stated without subtraction).
nodes.title: Number of members of a binary hierarchy

nodes.summary: The split of a binary character: the taxa in state `true`.
nodes.title: Split of a binary character

nodes.summary: The cluster of a vertex `v` seen from `a` is the side of `v` of the edge from `v` to its neighbor `p` toward `a`.
nodes.title: Clusters seen from a leaf are edge sides

nodes.summary: Compatibility depends only on the split, not on the side used to store it.
nodes.title: Compatibility is unchanged by complementing the first split

nodes.summary: Compatibility depends only on the split, not on the side used to store it.
nodes.title: Compatibility is unchanged by complementing the second split

nodes.summary: For the sides not containing a fixed taxon `a`, compatibility is being nested or disjoint: splits seen from a root are clusters.
nodes.title: Compatible clusters are nested or disjoint

nodes.summary: Two binary characters give compatible splits iff they do not show all four gametes (Buneman 1971; Estabrook, Johnson & McMorris 1976).
nodes.title: The four-gamete test

nodes.summary: Any two splits of one tree are compatible.
nodes.title: Edge splits of a tree are pairwise compatible

nodes.summary: Any two splits of one tree are compatible.
nodes.title: Splits computed from a leaf are pairwise compatible

nodes.summary: The splits `A | Aᶜ` and `B | Bᶜ` are compatible: one of `A ∩ B`, `A ∩ Bᶜ`, `Aᶜ ∩ B`, `Aᶜ ∩ Bᶜ` is empty (Semple & Steel 2003, Section 3.1).
nodes.title: Compatible splits

nodes.summary: The two sides of an edge are complementary.
nodes.title: The two sides of a tree edge are complementary

nodes.summary: `T` displays the quartet `xy|zw`: some edge split of `T` has `x, y` on one side and `z, w` on the other.
nodes.title: Tree displaying a quartet

nodes.summary: The cluster system `H` displays the triplet `xy|z`: some cluster contains `x` and `y` but not `z`.
nodes.title: Cluster system displaying a triplet

nodes.summary: The side of the edge `p – v` containing `v`: the taxa whose leaf is closer to `v` than to `p`.
nodes.title: Side of a tree edge containing a vertex

nodes.summary: The edge splits of `T`: the sides of all its edges (both sides of every edge).
nodes.title: Edge splits of a tree

nodes.summary: A rooted binary tree is determined by its triplets (Semple & Steel 2003, Theorem 6.4.1): two binary hierarchies on `S` displaying the same triplets are equal.
nodes.title: A rooted binary tree is determined by its triplets

nodes.summary: Every family of pairwise nested-or-disjoint nonempty subsets of a nonempty `S` is contained in a binary hierarchy on `S`, the cluster set of a rooted binary phylogenetic tree on `S` (Semple & Steel 2003, Proposition 3.5.2 and the refinement of a rooted tree to a binary one).
nodes.title: Hierarchies are refined by binary trees

nodes.summary: Perfect phylogeny and the four-gamete condition (Estabrook, Johnson & McMorris 1976; Gusfield 1991): a binary character matrix on at least two taxa has a perfect phylogeny iff no two of its columns show all four gametes.
nodes.title: Perfect phylogeny and the four-gamete condition

nodes.summary: The majority splits are clusters of one unrooted binary phylogenetic tree (a binary refinement of the majority-rule consensus tree).
nodes.title: The majority-rule consensus tree

nodes.summary: UPGMA always completes: from the singletons it reaches the single block `univ`.
nodes.title: UPGMA always completes

nodes.summary: The binary characters `χ` and `ψ` show all four gametes `(0,0), (0,1), (1,0), (1,1)` on the taxa.
nodes.title: Four-gamete condition for binary characters

nodes.summary: Ultrametrics satisfy the four-point condition (Semple & Steel 2003, Section 7.2), so every ultrametric on a finite set is a tree metric (`IsUltrametric.isTreeMetric`).
nodes.title: Ultrametrics satisfy the four-point condition

nodes.summary: The Aho graph of the triplets `R` on `S'` (vertices `S'`, an edge `x y` for each `xy|z ∈ R` with `x, y, z ∈ S'`) has a cut: a partition of `S'` into two nonempty parts with no edge across, i.e. the graph is disconnected.
nodes.title: Cut in the Aho graph

nodes.summary: `d` is the metric of a dated rooted tree, encoded by its clusters: a hierarchy `H` on the taxa with dates `h` (`0` at the leaves, strictly increasing from a cluster to any cluster strictly containing it) such that `d x y` is the date of the smallest cluster containing `x` and `y` (their most recent common ancestor). With edge lengths `(h D - h C) / 2` from each cluster `C` to its parent `D`, `d x y` is the path…
nodes.title: Metric of a dated rooted tree

nodes.summary: A binary hierarchy is a hierarchy.
nodes.title: A binary hierarchy is a hierarchy

nodes.summary: Adding `S` and the singletons to a family of pairwise nested-or-disjoint nonempty subsets of a nonempty `S` gives a hierarchy.
nodes.title: Pairwise nested-or-disjoint clusters form a hierarchy

nodes.summary: A hierarchy on a finite set `S`: a family of nonempty subsets of `S` containing `S` and every singleton, any two members nested or disjoint. These are the cluster systems of the rooted phylogenetic trees on `S` (Semple & Steel 2003, Section 3.5).
nodes.title: Hierarchy on a finite set

nodes.summary: `T` is a perfect phylogeny for the binary character matrix `M` (taxa by characters): the split of every non-constant column is a split of `T`, i.e. every character changes state on exactly one edge.
nodes.title: Perfect phylogeny for a binary character matrix

nodes.summary: Every ultrametric on a finite set is a tree metric (via Buneman's four-point theorem).
nodes.title: Every ultrametric is a tree metric

nodes.summary: Ultrametrics are dated tree metrics (Semple & Steel 2003, Theorem 7.2.5): on a nonempty finite set of taxa, a dissimilarity satisfies the three-point condition (and is a metric) iff it is the metric of a dated rooted tree.
nodes.title: Ultrametrics are dated tree metrics

nodes.summary: `d` is an ultrametric on the taxa: symmetric, zero exactly on the diagonal, and satisfying the three-point condition `d x z ≤ max (d x y) (d y z)` (equivalently, of the three distances among any three taxa the two largest are equal).
nodes.title: Ultrametric on taxa

nodes.summary: An unrooted binary tree is determined by its quartets (Semple & Steel 2003, Corollary 6.3.8): two trees displaying the same quartets are isomorphic. Already the quartets containing the taxon `a` suffice; they are the rooted triplets seen from `a`.
nodes.title: An unrooted binary tree is determined by its quartets

nodes.summary: The majority splits of a finite family of trees `T i`: the clusters, seen from `a`, of more than half of the trees (repetitions in the family count).
nodes.title: Majority splits of a family of trees

nodes.summary: Majority splits are compatible (Margush & McMorris 1981): two clusters each in more than half of the trees are both clusters of a common tree (pigeonhole), hence nested or disjoint.
nodes.title: Majority splits are compatible

nodes.summary: The clusters seen from `a` do not contain `a`.
nodes.title: Clusters seen from a leaf omit that leaf

nodes.summary: A split has bootstrap support above one half iff it is a majority split of the bootstrap replicate trees; so the splits with support above one half are pairwise compatible and form one tree (`exists_tree_majoritySplits_subset`).
nodes.title: Bootstrap support above one half means a majority split

nodes.summary: The Robinson–Foulds distance is symmetric.
nodes.title: Symmetry of the Robinson–Foulds distance

nodes.summary: The Robinson–Foulds distance is invariant under isomorphism, so it is a metric on the trees up to isomorphism.
nodes.title: Isomorphism invariance of the Robinson–Foulds distance

nodes.summary: The Robinson–Foulds distance does not depend on the leaf used to compute it.
nodes.title: Robinson–Foulds distance is independent of the base leaf

nodes.summary: The Robinson–Foulds distance vanishes exactly on isomorphic trees (Robinson & Foulds 1981).
nodes.title: Robinson–Foulds distance vanishes exactly on isomorphic trees

nodes.summary: On `n ≥ 3` taxa it is at most `2 (n - 3)`, the number of nontrivial splits of two binary trees (Robinson & Foulds 1981).
nodes.title: Maximum of the Robinson–Foulds distance

nodes.summary: The Robinson–Foulds distance from a tree to itself is zero.
nodes.title: Robinson–Foulds distance from a tree to itself is zero

nodes.summary: The Robinson–Foulds distance satisfies the triangle inequality.
nodes.title: Triangle inequality for the Robinson–Foulds distance

nodes.summary: The Robinson–Foulds distance: the number of splits in exactly one of the two trees. Each split is counted once, by its side away from the leaf `a` (its cluster seen from `a`); trivial splits are common to all trees and cancel. The value does not depend on `a` (`rfDist_eq_rfDist`).
nodes.title: Robinson–Foulds distance

nodes.summary: The split set computed from any leaf is the set of edge splits.
nodes.title: Split set from any leaf equals the edge splits

nodes.summary: The split set does not depend on the leaf used to compute it.
nodes.title: The split set does not depend on the leaf used to compute it

nodes.summary: The split set of `T` computed from the leaf `a`: both sides of every cluster of `T` seen from `a`. It equals `edgeSplits T` for every `a` (`splitSet_eq_edgeSplits`).
nodes.title: Split set of a tree computed from a leaf

nodes.summary: Splits-equivalence theorem, binary form (Buneman 1971; Semple & Steel 2003, Theorem 3.1.4): on at least two taxa, a family `F` of proper splits (both sides nonempty) is contained in the split set of some unrooted binary phylogenetic tree iff its members are pairwise compatible. The tree is a binary refinement of the tree whose splits are exactly `F` and the trivial ones.
nodes.title: Splits-equivalence theorem

nodes.summary: Compatibility is symmetric.
nodes.title: Symmetry of split compatibility

nodes.summary: A rooted triplet `xy|z`: `x` and `y` are closer to each other than to `z`.
nodes.title: Rooted triplet

nodes.summary: Each split is counted twice in the symmetric difference of the split sets (once per side), so the Robinson–Foulds distance is half of it.
nodes.title: Robinson–Foulds distance as half the split symmetric difference

nodes.summary: In every UPGMA run on an ultrametric, the recorded height of two taxa in the same block is their distance. In particular a completed run (one block) reconstructs `d`, i.e. the dated tree, exactly (Semple & Steel 2003, Section 7.2).
nodes.title: UPGMA is exact on ultrametrics

nodes.summary: The states reachable by UPGMA (Sokal & Michener 1958) on `d`: a partition `P` of the taxa into blocks and the heights `c x y` recorded so far. It starts from the singletons; each step merges two distinct blocks `C`, `D` of least average linkage (ties broken arbitrarily) and records `avgDist d C D` as the height at which every `x ∈ C` and `y ∈ D` are joined (the distance between them in the output tree; their common…
nodes.title: States reachable by UPGMA

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
